finding.summary: When len(unique_block_sizes) != 1: wbc_matmul only supports a single block size for the weight tesa. If the weighted block cover (driven by the caller's sparsity pattern / TeSA values) selects more than one block size, decompose_blocked_tesas is a no-op stub (`...`) and then a bare `raise` aborts the whole transformation. So a sparsity pattern that mixes block sizes is rejected rather than hand...
finding.review_note: blind review by an LLM subagent (round 1), not human: wbc_matmul hits a bare raise whenever the weighted block cover picks more than one block size (including a block size plus the (1,1) leftover), so mixed-granularity sparsity patterns from the user's TeSA are rejected.
